Package neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.flashops

Class TPHybridEosGeFlash

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.BaseOperation
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.flashops.Flash
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.flashops.TPflash
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.flashops.TPmultiflash
neqsim.thermodynamicoperations.flashops.TPHybridEosGeFlash
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable, OperationInterface
public class TPHybridEosGeFlash extends TPmultiflash
Dedicated multiphase strategy for EOS-gas, EOS-oil and GE-aqueous phase topologies.

The strategy reuses the general multiphase fugacity and phase-fraction equations, but starts from model-owned fixed creation-order roles and disables phase-discovery logic that can replace those roles with clones of the wrong phase implementation. Phase disappearance only changes the active phaseIndex mapping; a later flash restores the original gas, oil and aqueous objects through HybridEosGeFlashModel.prepareHybridEosGeFlash().

NeqSim

    • updateCoupledOverallComposition

      private void updateCoupledOverallComposition(int aqueousPhaseNumber, double[] oldAqueousMoles)
      Capture the reaction-adjusted species inventory before the next interphase-equilibrium solve.

      Chemical reactions conserve elements but change species amounts. The ordinary overall z values retain the feed species inventory, so using them here would remove bicarbonate, carbonate and other generated species during the next beta/composition update. The coupled inventory starts from the exact overall species amounts and applies only the mole changes produced by aqueous chemistry. It deliberately does not reconstruct the inventory from the latest phase split, because repeating that operation would accumulate the phase solver's finite material-balance residual. Synchronizing the exact inventory and its total preserves elements and charge while allowing reactions to change the total number of species moles.

      Parameters:
      aqueousPhaseNumber - active aqueous phase number
      oldAqueousMoles - aqueous component amounts before chemical equilibrium

    • getConservativeReactionDeltas

      private double[] getConservativeReactionDeltas(int aqueousPhaseNumber, double[] oldAqueousMoles)
      Project the aqueous reaction update onto the stoichiometric conservation null space.

      The chemical solver is iterative, so its raw mole update can contain a small component normal to the element and charge constraints. Reusing that update in an outer phase/chemistry loop would accumulate the residual. The projection delta - A+ A delta retains only reaction directions satisfying A delta = 0.

      Parameters:
      aqueousPhaseNumber - active aqueous phase number
      oldAqueousMoles - aqueous component amounts before chemical equilibrium
      Returns:
      conservative overall component mole changes
